home.diverge_h: When histories diverge, it stops and asks.
home.diverge_lead: The backup only accepts fast-forward pushes. If the source was force-pushed, BareKeep keeps the backup as it is, pauses automatic sync for that mirror, and lets you decide whether to overwrite it from the source.
home.route_label: The path of a diverged mirror: the source was force-pushed, this Mac is up to date, and the push to the backup is held.
home.msg: The backup has commits this mirror doesn’t have, so BareKeep didn’t push. Check the backup, or overwrite it from the source.
home.lamps_lead: The shape tells you the state, so you can read it without relying on color.

items.a: A macOS menu bar app that keeps mirrors of your GitHub, GitLab, Gitea and Forgejo repositories on your Mac, and can push them to your own Git server as an off-site backup. Each mirror is a complete Git repository you can clone from at any time.

A Mac with macOS 26.0 or later, and Git. BareKeep uses the Git that comes with macOS; if the Command Line Developer Tools are missing, BareKeep shows a page that installs them for you (about 1 GB, from Apple). Mirrors and settings are untouched while Git is missing, and syncing resumes once it is installed.

items.q: Do I have to pay for BareKeep?
items.a: BareKeep has a free plan that manages up to 3 mirrors, and Pro, a one-time purchase (no subscription) with no such limit. One Pro license covers every 1.x version. See Pricing.

items.q: Can I use BareKeep on more than one Mac?
items.a: Yes. The free plan works on every Mac you own or control. A Pro license key can be active on 2 of your Macs at a time; to use it on another one, deactivate it in Settings › License on one of the two first.
Yes, within 14 days of buying Pro, with no reason needed. The rules are in the Refund Policy.

items.q: What happens to my mirrors if my license stops working?
items.a: Nothing you have already mirrored or backed up is deleted, and the mirrors on your disk stay readable. BareKeep goes back to the free plan: the first 3 mirrors keep syncing, and the others stay where they are but are not synced until you upgrade.

items.q: Does BareKeep change my repositories on GitHub or GitLab?
items.a: No. Data only flows source, then this Mac, then backup. BareKeep never pushes to the source.

GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo (including codeberg.org), self-hosted instances of the last three, and any https Git URL. Add a self-hosted instance in Settings › Platforms first; after that it can be a source or a backup target.

Start with the run log and the status card of the mirror that has the problem: they explain failures in plain words. If that does not help, email support@barekeep.com and say what the status card shows. Never send an access token.

Sync Now runs a mirror immediately; a schedule runs them automatically. Failed runs retry with backoff, and the run log and each run’s output are on the mirror’s detail page. Pause Sync stops automatic runs; manual sync still works.

Add one or more backup targets (Gitea, Forgejo, GitLab or GitHub) and choose per mirror which ones it pushes to. Where the platform has an API, BareKeep creates the private repository for you. Backup is optional: without a target, the mirror stays on this Mac.

The backup has commits this mirror doesn’t have, for example after the source was force-pushed. To avoid overwriting them BareKeep does not push, and pauses automatic sync for that mirror. Check the backup, or choose Overwrite from Source… to reset its branches and tags to match the source. Commits that exist only in the backup are no longer referenced, so copy the local folder first if you want to keep them.

items.q: Where is my access token stored?
items.a: Only in your Mac’s keychain, one entry per source and per backup target. It is not written to files or logs and does not appear in command lines or environment variables; it is handed to git through a pipe.

No telemetry, no crash reports, no account. The only data BareKeep sends is the update check and, if you buy Pro, your license key and a device label to the payment provider. The Privacy Policy lists every address BareKeep connects to.

BareKeep checks for new versions once a day and when you ask (turn the daily check off in Settings) and installs them in the app after you confirm. Updates are free on both plans. The history of each version is on the Changelog.

privacy.lead: BareKeep does not collect or upload any data about you or your usage: no telemetry, no crash reporting, no account system.

sections.body:
To activate, verify or deactivate Pro, BareKeep sends the license key and a device label (your Mac’s name plus a short code derived from a hardware identifier) to Dodo Payments over HTTPS. Nothing else is sent to us or to the payment provider.

BareKeep has no accounts, no analytics, no crash reporting and no servers of its own. Its other request to us is the update check described below.

BareKeep does not collect or receive your repositories, your access tokens, your mirror list, your backup servers, or how you use the app. Everything runs on your Mac and on the servers you chose.

Logs stay on your Mac. Exporting diagnostics creates a file that you send yourself; tokens are removed from it. It does include the mirror list (repository addresses and local paths), so check it before you share it.

• The Git servers you configure: GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo or any https Git server, which the system git fetches from and pushes to. A token is sent only to the host it was created for, over https. Their own privacy policies apply.
  • Platform APIs: when you add a self-hosted instance, BareKeep probes the server kind without credentials (only the version endpoint is requested). A backup target’s connection test and automatic repository creation call that platform’s API.
  • dl.barekeep.com: to check for a new version of BareKeep, once a day unless you turn off the daily check, and when you ask. The request carries the app name and version, the update framework’s version and your IP address, and no system profile. An update is downloaded only after you confirm it, and installed only if its Apple signature and BareKeep’s EdDSA signature both verify.
  • Dodo Payments: our payment provider and the merchant of record. At checkout Dodo collects your name, email address and billing details under its own privacy policy, and handles invoices, taxes and refunds. BareKeep does not receive your payment details.
  • This website: static, with no analytics and no cookies. It and the downloads are served by Cloudflare, which keeps standard access logs.
  • Your browser: links such as “Open on …” are opened by the system browser.

• Your Pro license key is kept in your Mac’s keychain, as are access tokens.
  • Access tokens are kept only in your Mac’s keychain, one entry per source token and per backup target token. They are never written to files or logs and never appear in command-line arguments or environment variables; they are handed to the git subprocess through a pipe.
  • The mirror list, backup targets and run history are JSON files in ~/Library/Application Support/BareKeep; they contain no tokens. Logs are in ~/Library/Logs/BareKeep, with secrets removed before they are written.
  • Mirror repositories are stored in the folder you specify.

You can deactivate your license in Settings › License at any time. Deleting a mirror or removing a backup target deletes its keychain entry. After uninstalling BareKeep you can delete the folders and keychain entries above.

The developer can see your purchase record (name, email address, payment ID) in the Dodo dashboard, only to give support and process refunds. To ask what we hold, or to have it corrected or deleted, email support@barekeep.com; we reply within 30 days. If you are in the EU or the EEA, you also have the rights the GDPR gives you, including the right to complain to your local data protection authority.
If this policy changes, the date above changes with it.
